#### What's the first thing to check after a car accident?

#### 1. CHECK: "Is anyone hurt?"

- If you or any passengers are injuried, call 9-1-1 or ask someone else to call. 
- If you're seriously injured, try not to move, and wait for emergency personnel.
- If you or any passengers have neck or back pain, stop the injured person from moving and wait for first responders to arrive.

#### How do I get to safety after a car accident?

#### 2. GET TO SAFETY.
- If you're able to, move to the side of the road or a sidewalk.

- If your car is safe to drive and is causing a hazard where it is, pull it to the side of the road. Otherwise, leave it where it is and get yourself and your passengers to safety.

#### When should I call 911 after a car accident?

#### 3. Call 9-1-1
- Call if there is a fire concern
- To make a collision report. Even in minor accidents, it may be legally required by your state and your insurance. 
- Use the HazAdapt Help button to get your location if in an unfamiliar place.

> If the police cannot come to you, you can go to the nearest police station and complete a report yourself.

#### What should I do while waiting for help after a car accident?

#### 4. Wait for help if needed. 
- Turn off your engine.
- Turn on your hazard lights.
- Use the road flares in your emergency car kit to warn other vehicles to slow down.

> **Do not leave the scene until help arrives.**
> If you have to go because you are being threatened or it is otherwise unsafe for you to be there, you should be on the phone to 911, explaining why you left and where you are going. Returning to the scene once first responders have arrived is your best strategy in this case. Doing anything else risks a citation or arrest for hit-and-run.

#### What information should I exchange with other drivers after a car accident?

#### Collect the Driver's
- Full name and contact information
- Insurance company and policy number
- Driver's license and license plate number
- Type, color, and model of vehicle
- Location of the accident

> **Tip:** Stay calm and avoid discussing fault when going over the facts with the other driver. You do not have to decide who is at fault at the scene.

#### How do I document a car accident scene?

#### Take pictures and or video of:

 - Your vehicle from different angles, showing the damage done to both cars.
 - The other car's license plate. 

#### Take down names
- Get the names and addresses of anyone involved, including any passengers in the other vehicle.
- Get the name and badge number of all responding officers.

- Get a copy of the police report.

#### What should I do if I witness a car accident?

#### First, Keep Yourself Safe 

1. Pull over to a safe area.
 2. Be far enough away from the accident to leave room for emergency vehicles and to ensure that you are not in any danger. 
3. Put on your hazard lights
4. Only exit your car if it's safe. If you're on a busy highway, it may be best if you remain in your vehicle.

#### Should I call 911 if I witness a car accident?

- If you are unsure if the situation is an emergency, you should call 9-1-1 and let the call taker determine if emergency help is needed. 
- Use hands-free or put your car in park before you use your cell phone. 
- Be prepared to describe the scene and give your location. Use the HazAdapt Emergency Help Button at the bottom of the screen for your current location while calling. 

- If the cars are smoking, be sure to mention that when calling emergency services.

#### How can I offer support to a car accident victim as a witness?

If you feel it's safe to get closer to the scene of the accident, you can go over to see how you might be able to help. You may be able to provide aid by:

- First asking the victim if they are hurt or need help. 
- If you see someone hurt, do not attempt to move them, that could make their injuries worse. Stay with the victim till authorities arrive to make sure any injured receives proper medical treatment. 

- Offering your phone so the victims can call relatives or friends.

- Setting up road flares from your car emergency kit to block off the accident area.
 - Your presence can defuse a possible argument between the drivers or prevent someone from trying to leave the scene. Just be mindful of your own safety, and try to stay calm.

#### Should I stay at a car accident scene as a witness?

- You can help the authorities and those involved by giving an account of what you saw. 
- If someone is hurt or scared, you can act as a source of comfort until someone else arrives. 

Once the police arrive they may ask you for your contact details in case there are any follow-up questions after the accident.

#### What should I do during a car accident if my kid is with me?

#### 1. Check yourself first- " Am I hurt or in danger?"

 - If so, call 911 immediately. 

 #### 2. Get to Safety 
 - Turn on your hazard lights
- Use the road flares in your emergency car kit to warn other vehicles to slow down.

#### 3. Once in a safer position, check on your child. 
- Are they hurt or in danger? If they show any signs of injury, call 9-1-1. 
- Keep the child in their booster seat unless it is not safe to do so. 
- If you are physically able to do so, then you may move toward your child to console them until responders arrive.
- If you cannot move toward them, talk to them and reassure them that you are there while you wait.

> **Keep Kids in Their Car Seat.**
> Unless it is dangerous to do so, experts suggest waiting on medical responders to pick up or move a child in a car seat. This may be the hardest piece of advice for parents, but improperly moving a child can worsen any and all injuries.

#### How do I monitor my child after a car accident while waiting for help?

#### 4. Monitor your child while you wait for help
- Apply first aid to your child as needed while they are in the car seat. 
- Even if you see no initial signs of pain, always allow the medical experts to do an examination (for you and your child).

#### What should I do during a car accident if my pet is with me?

#### 1. Check: "Is everybody ok?"
- First, check yourself, any human passengers, then your pet for injuries

- If any humans are injured, call 9-1-1 or ask someone else to call. 

- If you're seriously injured, try not to move, and wait for emergency personnel. 

#### 2. Get to safety.

- If you're able to, move to the side of the road or a sidewalk.

- If your car is safe to drive and is causing a hazard where it is, pull it to the side of the road. Otherwise, leave it where it is and get yourself and your pet to safety. 

#### 3. Once in a safer position, check on your pet. 

- Are they hurt or in danger? Apply life-saving first aid if needed. 
- If there any signs of injury, find emergency veterinary care. 

- If you are physically able to do so, then you may move toward your pet to console them until responders arrive. 

- If you cannot move toward them, talk to them and reassure them that you are there while you wait.

#### How should I handle a car accident with a disability?

#### 1. GET TO SAFETY
- Turn on your hazard lights and move your car to a safe location. If you cannot move your car, stay inside with your seatbelt on and wait for help to arrive.
- If you cannot move or need assistance, try to attract attention by honking your horn or waving your arms out of the window.

#### 2. CHECK: "Is anyone hurt?"
- Check yourself and any passengers for injuries.
- If you have a service animal with you, ensure they are safe and secure.
- Apply first aid if needed.

#### 3. CALL 911 and get medical help if needed.
- Make first responders aware of any disability or mental health condition that may impact how they provide care.
- Make a collision report. Even in minor accidents, it may be legally required by your state and your insurance.
Use the HazAdapt Help button to get your location if in an unfamiliar place.
- If the police cannot come to you, you can go to the nearest police station and complete a report yourself. 

> **Autism and Mental Health Tip:** Riding in an ambulance can be overwhelming. If a person with Autism or cognitive disabilities is injured and must ride in an ambulance, ensure they have familiar and comforting items (i.e., headphones, iPad, etc.) for the ambulance ride.

#### How do I check my mobility device after a car accident?

**It is normal to feel shaky or upset after a car accident.**
 If you are feeling shaken or upset, take some time to rest and talk to a friend or family member for support.
It may be a good idea to call a trusted person to be on the phone with you while you talk with the other drivers, police, or insurance agents.

**Check Mobility Devices**
- If you use a mobility device, such as a wheelchair, check to ensure it is still in good condition and not damaged.

#### How should I handle exchanging info and insurance with a disability after an accident?

**Address Other Drivers**
- Exchange information with the other driver, including names, phone numbers, insurance information, and license plate numbers.
- Ask for their contact information if there were any witnesses to the accident.
- Take photos of the damage to cars, the surrounding area, and any road signs or landmarks.
- Contact your insurance company immediately to report the accident and file a claim. They may be able to send a tow truck if needed. If they are providing a ride from the accident scene to another destination, let them know if accessible transportation is needed.
- Be patient and cooperative with the police and other officials investigating the accident.

#### What emergency items should I keep in my car for a car accident?

Most important items:
* A phone to call for help
* Well-maintained vehicle with working seatbelts
* First aid kit with wound supplies
* Proof of car insurance
* Flashlight

Other helpful items:
* Emergency kit
* Blankets
* Clean towels

#### What kind of car seat should my child use at each age?

#### Birth until age 2–4: Rear-facing car seats: 
- For the best possible protection, infants and toddlers should be buckled in a rear-facing car seat, in the back seat, until they reach the maximum weight and height limits of their car seat.

#### Until at least age 5: Forward-facing car seat
- After outgrowing the rear-facing car seat, use a forward-facing car seat until at least age 5.

#### Booster seat

- Once children outgrow their forward-facing car seat, they should be buckled in a belt-positioning booster seat, in the back seat, until seat belts fit properly. Seat belts fit properly when the lap belt lays across the upper thighs (not the stomach) and the shoulder belt lays across the chest (not the neck).

#### Only Seat Belts

- Children no longer need to use a booster seat once seat belts fit them properly. Seat belts fit properly when the lap belt lays across the upper thighs (not the stomach) and the shoulder belt lays across the chest (not the neck).

- Proper seat belt fit usually occurs when children are about 4 feet 9 inches tall and aged 9–12 years. Seat belt fit can vary by vehicle so check fit in all vehicles. For the best possible protection, keep children properly buckled in the back seat.

#### How do I protect my kids from car accident injuries?

#### Buckle all children aged 12 and under in the back seat.
- Buckle children in the middle seating position of the back seat when possible (using a lap and shoulder belt), because it is the safest position in the vehicle.
- Airbags can kill young children riding in the front seat. Never place a rear-facing car seat in front of an airbag.
- Buckle children in car seats, booster seats, or seat belts on every trip, no matter how short the trip.
- Set a good example and help protect everyone in the car by always using your seat belt.

#### How can I protect my pet in the car?

Most importantly: Ensure that your pet is secure inside of the vehicle with a responsible human at all times. 

- Keep pets in a crate while in the car.
- Line their crate with soft blankets.
- Install a back seat barrier.
- Use a dog seatbelt or harness.
- Do not let them hang out the window.
- Do not leave your pet in a parked car for an extended period of time. They may quickly get overheated or get stolen.

#### What symptoms should I watch for after a car crash?

Car accidents (even minor ones) can cause injuries that can take time to show symptoms. 

Seek a medical evaluation if you think you or your children are experiencing any of these serious symptoms:
- Headaches

- Back Pain

- Abdominal Swelling, Bloating, or Pain

- Alterations in Physical Function, Personality, or Emotions

#### What recovery actions should I take for my child right after a car accident?

#### 1. Call your child's pediatrician. 
If emergency room doctors had to care for your child after the incident, then it is important to update your child's pediatrician. They will help create a plan of continued care with you or refer you to other doctors if needed. 

#### 2. Monitor them Closely
Watch carefully for symptoms of injury in the days following the accident. 

#### 3. Get a new car seat. 
Car seats should be replaced after all moderate or severe accidents and after some minor accidents. A car seat that has been in a crash may be unable to provide adequate safety if another crash occurs.

##### The A minor accident is when ALL of the below occur:
> - ##### The vehicle was able to be driven away from the crash scene
> - ##### The door(s) closest to the car seat suffered no damage
> - ##### No passengers suffered injuries
> - ##### No airbags deployed
> - ##### No visible damage to the car seat

Seats should be replaced even if your child was not in the seat at the time of the accident. Parents should follow the manufacturer's instructions for further advice on replacements. If you no longer have the instructions, visit the company's website for a downloadable version or call customer service.

#### 4. Keep other caretakers informed. 
Any babysitters, daycare workers, or family should know what is happening, special care instructions, and how to alert you and the child's doctor if they see any signs of injury.

#### What signs of injury should I watch for in kids and babies after a car accident?

#### Signs of injury in kids and babies after car accidents

- More crying than normal
- Sleepiness
- The inability to be consoled
- Lack of interest in toys or play
- Lack of interest in eating, or any other change in behavior 
 
If any of these symptoms develop in the hours or days after the accident, then seek medical treatment for your child even if they were seen by a doctor soon after the crash.

#### How might my child's mental health be affected after a car accident?

These reactions may begin immediately or after a delay. This is part of a normal recovery process. 

- Sleep fitfully, talk in sleep, have nightmares, scream, cry out,

- Guilt

- Acting Younger

- Fear

#### What are common reactions parents have after a child's car accident?

#### Common Reactions in Parents 
- Guilt
- Anxious or over-protective
- Sleep disturbances
- Inconsistency with discipline or expectations
- Over-indulging or letting the child "get away with" things

You can help your child by showing acceptance of their feelings, reassuring them that they are safe now, and by being consistent with normal routines, discipline, and expectations so that they will feel secure.
